meta.revision_note: REBUILT from a PPR basis after league settings confirmed zero points per reception. The prior PPR ordering was the wrong basis and has been replaced.
meta.coverage: 200 players — covers all 16 rounds of a 10-team draft
meta.source_ordering: Bleacher Report Top 100 PPR (2026), reordered here for standard scoring
meta.reorder_note: The standard-scoring adjustments below are MY derivation, not a sourced standard board. One anchor is external: nflfantasyedge reports Gibbs at #1 and Robinson at #2 in both Half-PPR and Standard. Everything else follows from removing PPR leverage. Treat the direction of each move as sound and the exact magnitude as approximate.
meta.bye_week_note: 18 of 32 teams verified. Backfill the rest from the Yahoo API.

standard_scoring_adjustments.principle: With 0 PPR, value shifts to yardage volume and touchdowns. Players whose fantasy production is reception-count-driven lose the most; touchdown-dependent and high-volume rushers gain.

notable_risers.why: Pure rushing volume and touchdowns with no receiving drag. The single biggest beneficiary on this board.
Early-down and goal-line role; his value never depended on catches.
Touchdown-dependent grinder — exactly the profile standard scoring rewards.
Big-bodied red-zone target; scores on volume of touchdowns, not receptions.
Workhorse rushing volume plus goal-line work.
Goal-line role is the whole thesis, and it survives intact without PPR.

notable_fallers.why: A large share of his projection is reception volume, which is now worth nothing.
Slot profile — high catch count, modest yards per catch.
Close to a pure PPR asset. Minimal standalone value in this format.
Slot-heavy usage loses its scoring engine.
Still elite on yardage and targets, but the reception-volume edge that made him a top-8 PPR pick is gone.
Tight ends generally lose the most from removing PPR, since receptions are a large share of their scoring.

position_level_effects.TE: Loses the most as a position group. McBride and Bowers remain the clear top two, but the gap between them and streaming tight ends narrows.
position_level_effects.RB: Gains overall. With only 2 RB slots plus a flex, and RBs concentrating touchdowns, elite backs hold their value best.
position_level_effects.WR: Bifurcates. Downfield and red-zone receivers hold value; slot and possession receivers fall sharply.
position_level_effects.QB: Unchanged in relative terms. Standard 4-point passing TDs and one QB slot mean QBs should go later than raw point totals suggest. Rushing QBs keep an edge because rushing TDs are worth 6.

league_specific_strategy.draft_for_ceiling: 8 of 10 teams make the playoffs. In 2025 the champion ranked 7th in points scored, a 6-8 team finished runner-up, and the 11-3 scoring leader finished 3rd. Weekly consistency has almost no value. Prioritize league-winning upside over safe floors.
league_specific_strategy.shallow_lineup: Only QB/WR/WR/RB/RB/TE/FLEX/K/DEF start. Fewer WRs needed than a typical 3-WR league, which softens WR scarcity and raises the relative value of elite RB and TE.
league_specific_strategy.stream_k_and_def: Unlimited acquisitions with continual rolling waivers means kickers and defenses are freely replaceable weekly. Spend zero meaningful draft capital on them — this board deliberately excludes them.
league_specific_strategy.autodraft_plan: You intend to take picks 1-15 manually then autodraft the remainder. Rounds 15-16 are K/DEF territory anyway, so this costs you very little.

build.method: Blended consensus: mean of available source ranks, then additive injury penalties.

sources.br_standard: Bleacher Report top 100 PPR, converted to standard scoring
sources.rotoworld: NBC Sports / Rotoworld — 2026 Fantasy Football Top 200 Overall (published 2026-08-15)

caveats: Two sources is enough to cancel single-outlet outliers, not enough to be a true consensus.
Players ranked past ~100 come from the Rotoworld list only, which is PPR-leaning — their standard-scoring correction is weaker than the top of the board.
Injury penalties are fixed rank shifts encoding added risk, not projections.
Kickers and defenses are deliberately excluded; unlimited waivers make them streamable.

meta.note_on_dates: Source lists were retrieved 2026-08-14/15; injury overlay and blend applied 2026-08-18.
